images.note: Gorbachev beat: PRIMARY is a 1980s contemporary poster portrait (not a news photograph — document honestly); ALT is Gorbachev's May 1986 letter to Reagan (courtesy Ronald Reagan Library) on the Bulletin's INF Treaty virtual-tour page — a document, not a portrait.
images.title: Mikhail Gorbachev — 1980s poster portrait; and his May 1986 letter to Reagan

images.note: Reagan beat: PRIMARY is Reagan addressing the Bundestag, Bonn, 1982 (HdG); ALT is the Berlin Wall speech contact sheet, Brandenburg Gate, June 12, 1987 (Reagan Library) — a contact sheet (grid of frames, visually weaker) but thematically Tier-1: the script quotes the 'tear down this wall' speech.
images.title: Ronald Reagan — Bundestag address 1982; and Berlin Wall speech contact sheet 1987

images.note: Summit beat (Geneva 1985 / Reykjavik 1986): PRIMARY visually confirmed as Reagan and Gorbachev at Hoefdi House, Reykjavik, Oct 1986 (Wende Museum); ALT is the Geneva Summit contact sheet, Nov 20, 1985 (Reagan Library).
images.title: Reagan and Gorbachev — Reykjavik 1986; and Geneva Summit contact sheet 1985

images.note: INF Treaty beat (Dec 1987): PRIMARY visually confirmed as Reagan and Gorbachev together at a podium with the presidential seal, Soviet flag behind, on the Bulletin's INF Treaty virtual-tour page — image credit is Alamy (ALAMY_GX4Y82); rights check belongs to the coordinator. ALT is the INF treaty signing contact sheet, East Room (Reagan Library).
images.title: Reagan and Gorbachev — Washington Summit / INF Treaty, Dec 1987

images.alt_source: European Solidarity Centre (via Google Arts & Culture)
images.note: Solidarity beat: PRIMARY is Walesa, Gdansk, Aug 26, 1980 (Britannica) — note the script beat is 1989 ('Solidarity forced the Communists from power') but the available verified image is the 1980 strike; ALT is strikers' sleeping quarters during the sit-in strike (European Solidarity Centre, via Google Arts & Culture).
images.title: Lech Walesa and Solidarity — Gdansk strike 1980

images.note: Baltic Way beat (Aug 23, 1989): PRIMARY is the Lithuanian Central State Archives item LCVA 0-124901, photographer J. Juknevicius (via Archives Portal Europe; license badge RS-InC on page); ALT is Harald Leppikson's photo of the human chain near Tallinn (EFA.250.0.139849), visually confirmed: families with children, Estonian tricolor flags — note the ALT is image/webp format.
images.source: Archives Portal Europe / Lithuanian Central State Archives
images.title: The Baltic Way human chain — Aug 23, 1989

images.note: Berlin Wall opening beat (Nov 9, 1989): PRIMARY is celebrating people on/before the Wall at night with the Brandenburg Gate behind (HdG); ALT is the Bundesregierung's 'Chronik der Deutschen Einheit' photo: crowds on the graffiti-covered Wall before the Brandenburg Gate in daylight, German flag flying.
images.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall — Brandenburg Gate, Nov 1989

images.note: Schabowski beat ('immediately, without delay'): PRIMARY is Schabowski's actual handwritten note for the press conference (HdG collection); ALT is Bundesarchiv Bild 183-1989-1109-030 (Thomas Lehmann), full-res on the Bundesregierung's chronicle page: Schabowski on the podium at the Nov 9, 1989 press conference, cameras and journalists in the room.
images.title: Gunter Schabowski — handwritten press-conference note; and the Nov 9, 1989 press conference
